correctness.rationale: An explicit continuous S_n-invariant barycentric strong deformation retraction glues because different facets meet only at vertices. Connectivity and cycle rank of its middle-level graph are proved for all k>=2. The exact Q[S_n] cellular sequence, group-preserved orientations, and a two-step Pieri identity yield precisely the multiplicity-free Specht decomposition, with no unproved infinite extrapolation. Finite checks match each character at all 120 S5 and all 5040 S7 elements, plus rank k=4; they are supplementary only.

originality.rationale: The infinite odd-family equivariant retraction and full multiplicity-free Specht decomposition are distinct from the known nonequivariant sphere-wedge result, the stable-graph dihedral results, and previously indexed fixed-parameter neighborhood modules. Searches, full-text comparisons and explicit residual risks are documented; priority is not presented as externally certified.
residual_risks: The abstract-only 1988 middle-level primary source could conceivably contain an unreported cycle-space invariant; it was not claimed as full-text excluded.

Kozlov (2007), Proposition 17.28, was only identified and characterized through Nilakantan–Singh (2018), not independently reviewed in full. Only its known nonequivariant content is used for comparison.
The closest indexed representation research record was available as a source-specific summary, not its complete public package.
Exact cycle-space representation may appear in unindexed or differently named combinatorial representation literature. No literature search proves uniqueness.

value.rationale: The closed irreducible decomposition under the full symmetric group gives uniform, natural, and non-Betti information for every odd Kneser graph, from the canonical middle-level topology underlying Kneser graph coloring. It determines all permutation traces, shows k pairwise distinct three-row irreducibles occur once, and provides a canonical equivariant model. Known homotopy wedge and numerical ranks are expressly not priority claims; no artificial restricted parameter slice or unsupported downstream consequence is needed.
